newsitem.title: USA: GM passed peak plant changeover level.
newsitem.headline: GM passed peak plant changeover level.

text.p: General Motors Corp has passed the peak of plants involved in model changeovers, the company's top financial executive said Tuesday, which should help improve manufacturing efficiencies in the future.
However, some of those gains will be offset by higher engineering and overtime expenses, GM Chief Financial Officer Michael Losh told reporters on a conference call.
GM, which is in the middle of launching 15 new cars and trucks, had nine plants changing over to new models in the third quarter. That is expected to fall to seven in the fourth quarter, Losh said.
The launches are proceeding well, Losh said, as evidenced by the fact GM was able to produce 1,262,000 vehicles in the third period, 17,000 more than it had forecast.
Although launch costs are expected to decline over time, Losh cautioned the company will be spending more in such areas as advertising as those products come to market.
"You've got some pluses and some minuses," he said.

Including special items, GM reported total net income from continuing operations of $1.27 billion, up from $396.7 million in the 1995 third period. Losh said a slightly richer mix of trucks to cars helped those results.

He said the automaker is one-third of the way through switching three car plants to produce light truck products. Full-size van production at the Wentzville, Mo., plant has been achieved, and the company continues to make progress on converting Doraville, Ga., and Arlington, Texas.
"By early next year we will have three plants that used to be car plants that are making trucks," he said.
In general, he said GM's North American Operations (NAO) still needs to generate about $500 more per vehicle in profit to reach the company's goal of an average five percent net profit margin.

Excluding special items, NAO earned $208 per vehicle in the third quarter. NAO and the Delphi Automotive Systems combined had a net profit margin of 2.1 percent in the quarter, versus a net loss margin of 0.4 percent a year ago.
Losh declined to comment on the company's negotiations with the Canadian Auto Workers union, which launched a strike October 3, or the United Auto Workers union.
